Your iPhone gets hot on a wireless charger and charges slowly mainly because **wireless charging generates heat, and iOS automatically reduces charging speed to protect the battery when the temperature gets too high.**

A little warmth is normal. Excessive heat combined with very slow charging usually means something is reducing charging efficiency.

## 1. Why your iPhone gets hot

There are six common reasons:

1. **Wireless charging naturally generates heat.** Some energy is lost during wireless power transfer and becomes heat.
2. **Misaligned phone and charger.** If your iPhone isn't centered correctly on the charging coil, energy transfer becomes less efficient and generates more heat.
3. **Thick phone case.** Thick cases, metal accessories, magnetic attachments, or wallet cases can interfere with wireless charging.
4. **Low-quality or slow charger.** Older Qi chargers may deliver less power and take longer to charge.
5. **Using your phone while charging.** Gaming, video streaming, navigation, and other demanding apps generate additional heat.
6. **Hot surroundings.** Charging in direct sunlight, a hot car, or a poorly ventilated location can make the problem worse.

## 2. Why charging becomes so slow

Your iPhone has built-in thermal protection.

When the battery gets too hot:
- iOS reduces charging power.
- Charging may slow dramatically.
- Charging may temporarily stop altogether.
- Charging above 80% may be limited until the battery cools down.

This is intentional battery protection, not necessarily a hardware problem.

Apple also identifies low-power wireless chargers as a reason charging takes longer:

| Charger type | Charging performance |
|---|---|
| Older Qi (5W–7.5W) | Relatively slow |
| Qi (10W) | Moderate |
| MagSafe | Faster, depending on model |
| Qi2 | Faster, depending on model |
| Qi2.2 | Up to 25W on compatible devices |

Actual speeds depend on your iPhone model, charger, and power adapter.
